claims.proposition_evaluated: At its meeting of 2026-08-26, the Infrastructure Committee carried a motion reducing the time each approved public speaker could speak from the five minutes provided by section 38 of the Council Procedures Bylaw to a maximum of three minutes for that meeting, at a meeting for which between 60 and 80 entries on the committee's list had been approved to speak on item 7.6.
claims.interpretation_notes: Supported under the required primary measure: the bylaw sets a five-minute maximum, the committee carried a meeting-wide three-minute maximum for each approved speaker, and the item 7.6 approved-speaker list has 64 entries. The motion passed 6–0; the minutes list six committee members, so the recorded vote meets the bylaw's two-thirds-of-all-members threshold (two-thirds of six is four). Required alternatives: N=64 is Supported under the 50–90 band; N-all=79 is Supported under both bands; N-spoke=52 is Partially supported under the primary 60–80 band and Supported under the 50–90 band. The finding is definition-sensitive because using recorded presentations instead of approved entries changes the primary-band row. These are counts of entries, not verified distinct people. The motion set a maximum; the minutes do not establish how long any speaker actually spoke.

supporting_evidence.finding: Section 38(1) of Bylaw 18155 provides a five-minute maximum for each approved speaker. The consolidation is dated 2025-10-29 and its amendment list and section annotations show no later amendment to section 38 in that consolidation.

supporting_evidence.establishes: The standing maximum in the supplied consolidation is five minutes per approved speaker.

limitations: The minutes and bylaw evidence was supplied as carried text in this package and read on 2026-10-02. The carried text is not an independent live retrieval; I did not verify the live meeting page, later approval status, or later corrections to items 1.4, 2.3 or 7.6.

The carried minutes replace every public speaker's name with the same label, so entries cannot be matched across lists. N, N-all and N-spoke are entry counts; distinct-person counts and the number approved but not recorded as presenting cannot be calculated from this text.

The motion's vote and coverage are established by the minutes, but no reason for the motion is recorded in the carried items. The queue count does not establish why the motion was moved or what speakers thought about the programme.
The carried pages do not provide a systematic review of earlier committee and Council meetings for section 38 adjustments. No conclusion about how common this kind of adjustment was is made here.

Section 3(c) of Bylaw 18155 says an establishing bylaw prevails in case of conflict. The text of Council Committees Bylaw 18156 was not included in the carried materials, so I did not independently assess whether it contains a conflicting procedure.

calculations_needed: N, approved entries on item 7.6: 15 + 15 + 15 + 15 + 4 = 64. Organization-bearing entries: 2 + 8 + 3 + 2 + 0 = 15.

N-all: item 7.1 = 5; item 7.3 = 1; item 7.4 = 8 in the Requests to Speak motion plus 1 additional speaker = 9; item 7.6 = 64. Total: 5 + 1 + 9 + 64 = 79 entries. A person approved on two items would be counted twice.
N-spoke on item 7.6: panel entries 16 + 16 + 18 + 2 = 52. Organization-bearing entries: 5 + 6 + 1 + 0 = 12.
Under the 60–80 band: N=64 Supported; N-all=79 Supported; N-spoke=52 Partially supported. Under the 50–90 band: all three counts are Supported.
Special-resolution threshold: the minutes list six committee members; two-thirds of six is four. The motion received six votes in favour.
